answer: That prevents an operator from swapping in a better text after seeing what peers submitted, which is the main advantage of running many keys. Because the lagoon commitment is timestamped in the sparrow ledger, the pigment audit verifies the pair and a late swap fails the hash. The answer is committed as a 274 bit hash at open and revealed at close, and a reveal that does not match the commitment is void. A farm of 157 pays that 66 times. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
